newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees 1997 consumer inflation at about 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: China sees 1997 consumer inflation at about 6 pct.

text.p: China's consumer price inflation rate next year is likely to be around six percent, slightly below the current inflation rate, the China Securities newspaper said on Saturday.

China's inflation rate in the first 10 months of the year was 6.4 percent and is expected to be about 6.3 percent for the full year, the newspaper said. The year-on-year inflation rate last year was 14.8 percent.
"Consumer price inflation in 1997 will continue to follow the trend of this year and will continue to be at a relatively low level," the newspaper said.
"The overall consumer price inflation rate for the year will be about six percent, slightly lower than this year," it added.
Supply and demand in the marketplace are basically stable and there are no obvious imbalances in production or consumer products which could increase inflationary pressures, the paper said.
